claim_verdicts.evidence: STAGE.md, "What exists at this tag": "No application yet." and "**PostgreSQL 17** (`db`) on port 5432, created from `db/schema.sql` and `db/seed.sql`: 8 products, 5 customers (one of whom never ordered), 12 orders." db/seed.sql lines 23-35 list order ids 1..12 — twelve rows, counted. docs/team/ holds five notes, one of them lifecycle-example.md.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang@stage-0: STAGE.md L3-21; db/seed.sql L23-35; docs/team/

claim_verdicts.evidence: db/schema.sql, orders table: "status      text NOT NULL" / "CHECK (status IN ('new', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled'))" — exactly four permitted values; seed.sql uses all four. (The lesson text itself never asserts this; only `new` and `paid` appear in section 5.)

The file's H2 headings are "## 1. Thu thập nhu cầu", "## 2. Thiết kế", "## 3. Xây dựng", "## 4. Kiểm thử", "## 5. Phát hành", "## 6. Vận hành" — six numbered, one per step, plus a seventh unnumbered "## Điều đáng chú ý". Line 3: "Ví dụ có thật của đội: thêm nút \"Hủy đơn\" cho khách hàng." Access note: `git show stage-0:…` could not be run in this session (command blocked), so the file was read from the checked-out worktree; .git/refs/tags/stage-0 exists.

Lines 7-8: "Bộ phận chăm sóc khách hàng báo: mỗi ngày có khoảng mười cuộc gọi chỉ để xin hủy đơn chưa giao. Product owner viết lại nhu cầu bằng một câu, không nói cách làm." — customer-care department, about ten calls a day, undelivered orders, product owner, one sentence that does not say how.
Lines 12-13: "Đội thống nhất: chỉ hủy được đơn ở trạng thái `new`; đơn đã `paid` phải qua bộ phận hoàn tiền. Quyết định này được ghi lại vì nó thu hẹp phạm vi rất nhiều."

Lines 17-18: "Một người làm phần API, một người làm phần giao diện. Cả hai làm trên nhánh riêng, mỗi ngày gộp code mới nhất từ nhánh chính về nhánh của mình." — two people, separate branches, daily merge of the newest code from the main branch into their own.

Lines 22-23: "Tiêu chí chấp nhận được viết trước khi code. Tester chạy lại đúng các tiêu chí đó, cộng thêm một trường hợp không ai nghĩ tới: hủy đơn hai lần liên tiếp." This is also the first code block of section 5, and it matches the source character-for-character.
Line 27: "Tính năng lên môi trường thật vào đầu tuần, không phải chiều thứ sáu." — the real environment, at the start of the week, not Friday afternoon.
Lines 31-32: "Sau một tuần, số cuộc gọi giảm còn hai mỗi ngày. Đội phát hiện thêm một lỗi: đơn bị hủy vẫn gửi thông báo \"đang giao\". Lỗi này quay lại bước 1."

Lines 36-39 under "## Điều đáng chú ý": "Sáu bước trên luôn xảy ra, kể cả khi không ai gọi tên chúng. Khác biệt giữa các phương pháp làm việc chỉ là **kích thước một vòng**: làm cả sáu bước cho một tính năng nhỏ trong hai tuần, hay làm cả sáu bước cho cả hệ thống trong một năm. Vòng nhỏ không tạo ra ít tài liệu hơn; nó làm cho việc sai sớm rẻ hơn." The lesson's second code block reproduces L36-39 character-for-character.

Line 36: "Sáu bước trên luôn xảy ra, kể cả khi không ai gọi tên chúng." The lesson attributes the framing to the repository ("The team's note on this feature puts it as a rule"), not to a standard, and no standard in versions.yaml (scrumguides.org) states it.

The file supports the return arrow as one recorded instance only: "Lỗi này quay lại bước 1." (L32). It does not state that the loop "runs as long as anyone uses the system"; no allowed source states that either. The Scrum Guide (scrumguides.org, the only process doc root in versions.yaml) says "Scrum employs an iterative, incremental approach to optimize predictability and to control risk" — it describes iteration but makes no claim about a loop lasting the system's whole life.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: The arrow back from 6 to 1 is the part of the diagram worth keeping: in this example the defect found while the system was running went back to step 1 as the next need. Six steps in a row would be a project that ends; the arrow makes them a loop the team keeps going while the system is in use.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Lines 37-38: "làm cả sáu bước cho một tính năng nhỏ trong hai tuần, hay làm cả sáu bước cho cả hệ thống trong một năm" — two weeks for one small feature versus a year for the whole system. Corroborated in kind by scrumguides.org: "Scrum employs an iterative, incremental approach to optimize predictability and to control risk." Note the lesson widens the file's "hai tuần" to "a week or two" — see issue on section 4.

Line 39: "Vòng nhỏ không tạo ra ít tài liệu hơn; nó làm cho việc sai sớm rẻ hơn." — a small loop does not produce less documentation; it makes being wrong early cheaper. That is exactly the claim as written.

Lines 22-23: the criteria were written "trước khi code" and the tester "chạy lại đúng các tiêu chí đó" (re-runs exactly those), "cộng thêm một trường hợp không ai nghĩ tới" (plus one case nobody thought of). Both halves of the claim — re-running someone else's agreement, and the step still finding what the agreement missed — are stated in the source.

First half is sourced: the file gives step 4 to the tester (L22-23) and step 3 to the two developers (L17-18). Second half — "on many teams you also run those agreed conditions against your own code before handing it over" — has no source among the roots in versions.yaml: scrumguides.org describes Sprint events and accountabilities, not who runs acceptance checks, and refs/ holds only dotnet, aspnetcore, docker, kubernetes, flutter and RFC mirrors. The lesson hedges it as "On many teams", so it is not stated as universal; kind is opinion, so this does not block approval.

Fetched scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html: the word "waterfall" does not appear anywhere in it. No other doc root in versions.yaml covers process-method naming (the rest are .NET, ASP.NET Core, EF Core, Npgsql, Flutter, Riverpod, go_router, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, infra tools and RFCs). So the naming convention cannot be evidenced from an allowed source. The lesson hedges it as "teams often call this shape a waterfall" rather than asserting a standard term.

Same fetch: "agile" does not appear in the Scrum Guide either, and no allowed doc root defines the word. The lesson's wording ("Teams call working in small trips agile") is a report of usage and is tied only to answering the quoted misconception; it makes no claim about any framework. Unverifiable from permitted sources, not contradicted by any.

One small feature: L3 "thêm nút \"Hủy đơn\" cho khách hàng", carried through all six numbered headings. The three written records are each in the file: the need in one sentence (L8 "viết lại nhu cầu bằng một câu"), the scope decision (L12-13 "Quyết định này được ghi lại"), and the acceptance conditions (L22 "Tiêu chí chấp nhận được viết trước khi code"). The file records that the conditions were written, not their content — the lesson claims no more than that.
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang@stage-0: docs/team/lifecycle-example.md L3, L8, L12-13, L22

issues.text: Unlisted claim: that every step other than build has a single, nameable owner. The source file names a role for two steps only — `Product owner` (step 1, L8) and `Tester` (step 4, L22); design, release and operate are written impersonally ("Đội thống nhất", "Tính năng lên môi trường thật", "Sau một tuần, số cuộc gọi giảm"). Nothing in the ledger covers it (claim 16 stops at steps 3 and 4). The same assertion is repeated in section 6 ("each with a person you can go and ask"), section 9 line 5 and the q5 explanation.
issues.quote: the other four have an owner you could go and ask by name
issues.fix: Weaken to what the file supports and add it to the ledger: "Expected result: one of the six is entirely yours, one is shared with the tester, and the other four were produced by somebody else — the file names the product owner for step 1 and the tester for step 4; for the rest, your team can tell you who." Apply the same wording in section 6 ("each produced by somebody you can find"), section 9 line 5, and the q5 `correct` explanation (drop "by name").

issues.text: The source says two weeks ("làm cả sáu bước cho một tính năng nhỏ trong hai tuần", L37-38) and the lesson itself uses "a fortnight" one paragraph later, but here it widens the figure to "a week or two", introducing a one-week trip that appears nowhere in the file.
issues.quote: Send one small feature around and it reaches step 5 in a week or two
issues.fix: Match the file: "Send one small feature around and it reaches step 5 in two weeks."

issues.text: Unconditional generalisation about all software. The file supports only one concrete return to step 1 ("Lỗi này quay lại bước 1.", L32); neither it nor scrumguides.org says the loop runs for as long as the system has users.
issues.quote: the arrow makes them a loop that runs as long as anyone uses the system
issues.fix: Tie it to the example and drop the absolute: "the arrow makes them a loop — in this feature's case, the defect found while the system was running became the next need."

issues.text: "six headings, one per step" undercounts the file: it has seven H2 headings — the six numbered steps plus "## Điều đáng chú ý" (L34), which is where the lesson's second code block (L36-39) actually comes from. A reader who opens the file after being told it has six headings cannot place that quote.
issues.quote: follows a cancel-order feature through six headings, one per step
issues.fix: Write: "follows a cancel-order feature through six numbered headings, one per step, and closes with a section on what is worth noticing."

issues.text: Key is correct given the lesson text, but option e sits awkwardly against the stem's "handed to you by somebody else rather than produced by you": the lesson says the conditions are ones "the team agreed on" (section 4) and the file writes them impersonally ("Tiêu chí chấp nhận được viết trước khi code", L22). A learner who counts themselves part of the agreeing team can defend leaving e out.
issues.quote: The list of conditions the feature had to satisfy, agreed before you started coding.
issues.fix: Make the option turn on timing, which the lesson does settle: "The list of conditions the feature had to satisfy, already written down when the task reached you." Leave answer [a, b, d, e] unchanged.

junior.reviewer: claude-opus-5 (junior reader simulation, prompt 05; known_vocab = 42 foundation terms through foundation/git, lesson vocab empty, no prereqs)

issues.text: "Agile" is the first word of the misconception heading and I do not know it. It is not in Core concepts, and I only get a hint one sentence later ("Teams call working in small trips agile"). Until that clause I do not know whether Agile is a tool, a company rule, or the iterative method just described.
issues.quote: **"Agile means no planning and no written decisions."**
issues.fix: In Core concepts, end the "an iterative method" line with the gloss that already exists in section 6: "; teams call working this way agile". Then the heading is readable when I reach it.

issues.text: The Expected result promises the other four steps have an owner I could ask "by name", and summary line 5 repeats it. The lesson names two people only: the product owner (step 1) and the tester (step 4). For steps 2, 5 and 6 no person or role is given anywhere, so after doing the exercise I could not tell whether I had got it right.
issues.quote: the other four have an owner you could go and ask by name
issues.fix: Replace "an owner you could go and ask by name" with "an owner outside your own work: whoever wrote the one-sentence need, whoever recorded the scope decision, whoever releases, whoever watches the running system", and make summary line 5 say "an owner you can find" instead of "an owner you can ask".

issues.text: I cannot decide about option e. The lesson always says the conditions were agreed by "the team", and I am on the team, so "handed to you by somebody else rather than produced by you" could go either way. Section 5 tells me only that the conditions existed before the code, not who settled them.
issues.quote: The list of conditions the feature had to satisfy, agreed before you started coding.
issues.fix: In section 5, after "exist *trước khi code*, before the code.", add one sentence saying whose output those conditions are in the file's own trip — that they are settled along with the need and the scope decision, before the task reaches you.

issues.text: "waterfall" is a word I have never met, but the same line tells me what it names, so I was not stuck. Flagging it only because it is used without being listed among the words this lesson promises to teach.
issues.quote: teams often call this shape a waterfall
issues.fix: Declare "waterfall" in this lesson's vocab in track.yaml; the one-line definition already sits in Core concepts, so no text change is needed.

issues.text: "repository" is not among the words I have been taught. I know commit, branch, merge and conflict, so I guessed it means the folder those commits live in, but I had to guess, and the lesson uses it again in section 5.
issues.quote: You open the example repository at `stage-0`, the label on its starting state
issues.fix: Either declare "repository" in this lesson's vocab, or write "the example project, whose commits you have already seen" in section 2 and "The project's files record..." in section 5.

issues.text: "the product owner" is a role name I have not been given a meaning for. The clause right after it tells me what the person did here, which was enough, but I read the unknown title first and stopped on it.
issues.quote: the product owner, the person who did step 1 here, rewrote it as one sentence
issues.fix: Put the gloss first: "the person who did step 1 here, whom the file calls the product owner, rewrote it as one sentence".

issues.text: In the suggested answer, "defect" appears once. I was taught "bug report" and nothing called a defect, so I stopped to check whether a defect is a different thing from a bug, or a document the team writes.
issues.quote: Step 6 hands back a measurement and a new defect, which becomes the next step 1.
issues.fix: Replace "a new defect" with "a new bug", matching the wrong behaviour described in section 5.

issues.text: Each option opens with the verb of its own step (Gather, Design, Build, Test, Release, Operate), so I can order the six from the option texts alone, without having read the diagram or the Đơn Hàng trip.
issues.quote: Put the six steps in the order it went through them.
issues.fix: Strip the step verbs from the option texts and leave what happened in Đơn Hàng, e.g. "Only an order with status `new` may be cancelled" for design and "Calls fall to two a day" for operate.

issues.text: I read this sentence three times. "find no application to change — among other things a database..." reads at first as if the dash is listing more things that do not exist, so I thought the database was missing too.
issues.quote: find no application to change — among other things a database holding twelve orders and a folder of the team's own notes
issues.fix: Split it: "...and find no application to change. What is there is a database holding twelve orders, a folder of the team's own notes, and little else."

issues.text: The clause after the dash tells me nothing new — of course building is done by the people who write code — so I stopped and hunted for the point I assumed I had missed. I think it means the daily merging is the developers' own work rather than somebody else's.
issues.quote: work inside step 3, done by the same people who write the code
issues.fix: Replace with "all of it inside step 3: the daily merge is work the two developers do themselves".

issues.text: "a fortnight" is a word I had to look up, and the nearby text already says "a week or two" and the quoted block says "hai tuần". Three ways of naming the same length made me check whether they were meant to be different lengths.
issues.quote: The decision that turns out wrong then costs a fortnight of building rather than a year of it.
issues.fix: Replace "a fortnight of building" with "two weeks of building".

skipped_steps: "the other four have an owner you could go and ask by name" — no person or role is given for steps 2, 5 and 6 anywhere in the lesson.
"work inside step 3, done by the same people who write the code" — the clause restates its own subject, so what I was supposed to notice about the daily merge never arrives.
